end.summary:
• Practised ordering cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism; one unaided ordering was correct.
• Discussed human examples including muscle cell, muscle tissue, heart, digestive system and organism.
• Discussed plant examples: leaf as an organ; xylem and phloem as tissues; examples were not yet secure.
• Explained that blocked blood vessels can affect heart muscle and the whole body; this idea was partly explained independently.
• Organ versus organ system confusion was revisited, but not corrected after its last appearance.
end.parentNote: Yash practised ordering levels of organisation and linking examples across humans and plants. They used the method of building from smaller parts to larger ones, and later connected a blocked vessel to effects on heart muscle and the whole body. They still mixed up an organ with an organ system and needed support with xylem and phloem; the organ/system mix-up was not corrected after it last appeared. At home, ask Yash to make two columns—human and plant—and fill in one example for each level, including leaf, xylem and phloem.
